topics.label: Lecture introduction and framing
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the topic of complement, compares its complexity to the Krebs cycle, and sets expectations for the lecture.

topics.label: Fundamentals, nomenclature, and the central role of C3
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the foundational concepts of the complement cascade, explaining its general functions, naming conventions, and the pivotal role of component C3.

topics.label: Complement activation pathways and threshold
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the three biological pathways that recognize pathogens and trigger the deposition of C3b onto target surfaces.

topics.label: Effector mechanisms of complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the three primary downstream mechanisms through which the activated complement cascade clears pathogens and promotes inflammation.

topics.label: Complement regulation and host cell protection
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how host cells use regulatory proteins to prevent unintended self-damage by complement activation.

topics.label: Clinical impact of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines how genetic or acquired deficiencies in specific complement components result in distinct clinical disease presentations.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic analyzes the evolutionary strategies pathogens employ to evade complement destruction, focusing on Staphylococcus aureus.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and upcoming topic preview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the complement module and outlines the topic for the subsequent lecture.
